articleTitle: Measurements of the complex permittivity of microwave circuit board substrates using split dielectric resonator and reentrant cavity techniques
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The split dielectric resonator technique makes it possible to measure the real part of permittivity of isotropic materials for a very broad permittivity range and dielectric loss tangents in the range from 10/sup -4/ to 10/sup -1/ with high accuracy. For uniaxially anisotropic materials, the split resonator method permits measurement of the permittivity and and the dielectric loss tangent in the plane parallel to the the sample bottoms. Additional measurements using re-entrant cavity enable determination of permittivity and the dielectric loss tangent perpendicular to this plane.

articleTitle: A new model for electrical ageing and breakdown in dielectrics
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We derive a simple but generally applicable model for multi-factor ageing in which thermally-induced bond scission is a universal underlying physical process which determines ageing. The final destruction of the dielectric is assumed to occur by a Griffith-crack treeing process and this will have a formative time which will be part of the overall ageing time. Whether it will be a significant part will depend on t/sub c/ and therefore on the field E.

articleTitle: Non-linear fillers in electrical insulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: It is shown that in unfilled polyester, and that filled with Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/, the conductivity is Ohmic at low field strengths and space charge limited (SCL) at high fields. With ZnO, however, its non-linear, semi-conducting characteristic changes the conductivity of the filled polyester at sufficiently high concentrations. At low concentrations the characteristics of the polyester dominate but for higher concentrations there is a transition from SCL at low fields to tunnelling or Schottky emission across the inter-granular boundaries at high fields. Treeing tests are a practical demonstration of this phenomenon. Unlike Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/, which provides a barrier to tree growth due to its high adhesive bond and fracture toughness, ZnO provides an additional enhancement to tree resistance because of its non-linear properties and its ability to redistribute accumulated space charge.

articleTitle: Influence of carbon particles on the breakdown and partial discharge inception voltage of aged mineral based transformer oil
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper reports on experimental investigations dealing with the influence of carbon particles on the breakdown voltage of aged transformer oil in a temperature range between 20 and 110/spl deg/C and on the partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) at 20/spl deg/C. The oil samples were carbonized and afterwards subjected over periods of 1000 and 2000 h to different accelerated ageing conditions at 20 and 90/spl deg/C in the presence of metallic catalysts. The results reveal that the breakdown voltage of carbonized oil samples is slightly increased by the ageing whereas the PDIV experiences a significant improvement.

articleTitle: Electrical endurance characterization of polypropylene winding capacitors for traction applications: a new experimental method
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A method for testing patterned metallized film capacitors for DC applications is presented. Individual breakdowns in the capacitor can be detected by observing the leakage current. Capacitance of the charged capacitor and the amount of energy involved in clearings are obtained.

articleTitle: Pulse sequence analysis-what does it tell us about multiple discharge sites?
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Partial discharge analyses are widely used to get relevant information on the actual state of high voltage equipment. The standard partial discharge analyses are based on the phase angle distribution of the discharges and do not include the correlation between consecutive discharges thus neglecting physically relevant information. The Pulse Sequence Analysis considers especially the correlation between consecutive discharges and thus enables a more sophisticated evaluation.

articleTitle: Measurement of space charge distribution at high temperature using the pulsed electro-acoustic (PEA) method
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: To measure a space charge distribution at high temperature directly and accurately using the pulsed electro-acoustic method, temperature dependence of the output signals from two kinds of piezo sensor (PVDF, LiNbO/sub 3/) were checked, and the new system for measurement at high temperature was developed. The change of charge distribution with increase of temperature in a electron-beam-irradiated PMMA was observed using the new system as the typical measurement example.

articleTitle: Electric field enhancement within moulded samples of low density polyethene-a means of failure characterised by voltage ramp tests and space charge measurement
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The work reported here presents evidence that the stress enhancing factor operating is that of a space charge hetero-field which enhances the applied field at the electrode up to a value of /spl sim/1 MV/mm, which is sufficient to cause 'intrinsic' breakdown in polyethene. Here, breakdown would be caused by the effective elimination of the barrier to charge injection, causing a destructive injection current. This mechanism would also be consistent with the 'wormhole' breakdown structures typically observed for majority of ramp failures in the region of characteristic field.

articleTitle: Space charge accumulation and conduction current in XLPE insulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Space charge and conduction current measurements have been performed on XLPE insulation with semiconducting electrodes subjected to dc electrical fields between 20 and 70 kV/mm. It was found that the space charge accumulation in fresh insulation resulted in heterocharge distributions, which was attributed to the presence of curing by-products. In degassed insulation, the space charge accumulation resulted in homocharge distributions for the lower charging fields and an additional heterocharge accumulated near the cathode for the higher charging fields. The modification of the electrode electrical fields in degassed XLPE was found to be approximately half of that in fresh XLPE. On basis of conduction current measurements in degassed XLPE it was difficult to identify the controlling conduction mechanism(s) and to establish a clear correlation between the conduction current and space charge accumulation.

articleTitle: Failure mechanisms in film-based power capacitors
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Experience with all-film capacitors of both dry and oil impregnated types in power electronic equipment has been discussed from the users' viewpoint. The consequential results of failure can be considerable and, although capacitors have proved to be generally reliable devices, the wide variety of failures encountered have often been associated with batch manufacturing problems.

articleTitle: Partial discharge modelling and measurements on micrometer voids in solid dielectrics
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In this paper we present measured partial discharge current waveforms for micrometer voids in PTFE (teflon) and PC (polycarbonate). From the time-resolved partial discharge current waveforms detailed information on discharge mechanisms is obtained. The experimental studies show that the measured values for the inception voltage correspond well with calculated inception voltages based on the critical streamer criterion. The trends of externally measured quantities correspond with those predicted by our models and seem to hold their validity for micrometer voids.

articleTitle: Generalised frequency response applied to dielectrics
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The article demonstrates the recently introduced generalised frequency response technique developed for treating linear systems with time varying coefficients. The method is applied to determining the response of capacitor resistor systems with time varying dielectric loss where the loss spectrum has a 1/f character.

articleTitle: Conductivity and percolation in polymeric particulate composites of epoxy resin and conductive fillers
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Composites of the polymer-filler type, when the filler is a conductive material, show electrical conductivity at a significant volume concentration of the conductive phase and their behaviour can be described in terms of percolation theory. In these heterogeneous systems the constituents have markedly different properties and the ratio of the conductivities of the two components is /spl sim/10/sup 10/-10/sup 20/. These systems obey the relation of the percolation theory /spl sigma//spl sim/(P-P/sub c/)/sup /spl alpha// where /spl sigma/ is the electrical conductivity of the composite material, P is the filler concentration by volume, P/sub c/ its threshold value and /spl alpha/ the critical exponent. In this work, composites of epoxy resin and metal powders (Cu, Ni, Fe) or carbon black, in various volume fractions were prepared and their DC conductivities were measured. Data obtained by DC measurements are treated using percolation theory and values of P/sub c/ and /spl gamma/ are estimated through a suitable algorithm.

articleTitle: The effect of absorbed water on electrical treeing in epoxy resins
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The electrical tree growth behaviour in CY1300 and CT1200, the base resins used in switchgear and transformer bushings, have been examined after conditioning the samples over a range of temperature and relative humidity environments. The time to breakdown for both CY1300 and CT1200 samples stored in the laboratory or in water at 20/spl deg/C show the classic U-shaped dependence with sample age or moisture uptake. The anomalous diffusion model was found to be a good description of the experimental data over a wide range of temperatures and different relative humidity environments.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction phenomena through impregnated pressboard submitted to a thermal gradient
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: For the last twenty years, flow electrification has been suspected to be responsible of failures in high power transformers. In order to understand the phenomenon and to avoid incidents, several research programs have been undertaken in different countries. Our laboratory is involved in one of this program in collaboration with the French Electricity Company (E.D.F.). From this research in terms of velocity, pipe geometry, temperature and moisture content it seems that the transverse thermal gradient play a fundamental role in the process.

articleTitle: In-situ assessment of composite insulator surface condition
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Chemical surface analysis techniques have been applied to investigate ageing of HV composite insulators. A number of simple non-invasive techniques have been developed for sampling shed material of insulators in power systems. FTIR analysis of EPDM insulators has produced a measure of surface oxidation that indicates that oxidation is accelerated by the combination of electric field and UV. No such effects were observed from FTIR analysis of silicone rubber insulators, but it is possible that analysis of the silicone content of the surfaces using XPS and TGA will be useful techniques in determining the amount of LMW material remaining in the insulator. Further work is progressing to systematically examine how controlled amounts of UV and surface discharging affect surface condition as measured by these techniques. The further question of how the surface condition affects surface discharging also remains to be answered.

articleTitle: Measurement of space charge distribution in XLPE cables under AC stress
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In this paper we present a method for the determination of the space charge distribution, and hence the electric field distribution, in XLPE cables under an AC stress. The instrument has been developed from the well known pressure wave propagation (PWP) techniques, which have been successfully used in the study of materials under DC stress. Analysis demonstrates a high degree of confidence in the data. Data are reported, which show that statistically significant, at the 87% level, modification of the electric field due to the space charge occurs at the interfaces (in this case the semi conducting screens of the cable). The method described here will be useful for the study of high voltage AC insulation materials and structures. The technique is of particular interest for the nondestructive study of insulation ageing under AC electrification.

articleTitle: Application of dielectric and thermal analysis to the curing of epoxy resins
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Upon studying the application of dielectric analysis (DEA) to techniques for non-destructive on-line measuring of the curing process of epoxy casting resin in molds, it was found that the ionic conduction portion derived from dielectric loss factor was closely correlated to glass transition temperature and resin viscosity. A new study was undertaken using DEA, differential scanning calorimetry (DSC), dynamic mechanical analysis (DMA) and curing volume shrinkage measurement to investigate in more detail the relation between the electrical conductivity of resins and the degree of cure during the curing process. A relation was quantitatively determined between the equivalent resistivity derived from dielectric loss factor and the degree of cure, viscoelasticity and volume shrinkage.

articleTitle: Partial discharge stressing of filled epoxy resin surfaces
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The work described herein investigates the effect of both partial discharge and chemical/radiation stressing on a bisphenol-A epoxy resin which has had one of three fillers added. The three fillers selected for investigation were alumina (Al/sub 2/O/sub 3/), silica (SiO/sub 2/) and wollastonite (CaSiO/sub 3/). These three fillers were selected to cover the range of shape of particle and acidity of filler material commonly in use in industry today.

articleTitle: Dielectric selection for a robotic electrostatic gripping device
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Researchers have been applying electrostatic force to the handling and restraint of materials for a large part of the twentieth century. The principle has recently been applied to the robotic handling of non-rigid materials, for which it shows a number of advantages over other gripping methods. This paper introduces the concepts and requirements of electrostatic gripping of such materials, and then details selection procedures for dielectric materials. It is found that analysis of the gripping technique produces dielectric material requirements quite different from those expected from a preliminary study of the device. Implementation and manufacture of these robotic devices are then described for a potential application. A robotic cell has been constructed and integration of the electrostatic gripping device into the cell is detailed. The paper concludes with a summary of the scope, advantages and limitations of the resultant system.

articleTitle: The effect of hydrostatic pressure and temperature on the permittivity of crosslinked polyethylene
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The real part of the permittivity of crosslinked polyethylene cable insulation has been measured as functions of temperature and hydrostatic pressure. The results obtained are discussed in terms of the Clausius-Mosotti equation. The real part of the permittivity decreases with increasing temperature. The temperature dependence cannot be totally ascribed to the variation of density with temperature. This suggests that the polarizability of this crosslinked polyethylene decreases with increasing temperature, which is qualitatively consistent with a Debye model. The effect of applying hydrostatic pressure is to increase the real permittivity. Analysis of the effect of pressure on the dielectric behaviour on the basis of the Clausius-Mosotti model leads to a negative /spl part//spl alpha///spl part/P: the polarizability a of crosslinked polyethylene decreases with pressure. The major consequences of applying pressure are to reduce the free volume of the polymer, increasing the restricting force for free dipole rotation.

articleTitle: Salt-fog testing of composite insulators
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The results of salt-fog tests performed on silicone rubber insulators have been complemented by measurements of water droplet contact angle. The performance of these insulators was mostly inconsistent with service experience and this was attributed to the continuous nature of the test which inhibits the processes of rejuvenation for which silicone elastomers have become renowned. The validity of the salt-fog test in qualifying silicone insulators is questioned and proposals are made for alternative procedures.

articleTitle: Correlation between surface degradation and PD wave shape evolution for spherical voids
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The present study reports the recording of partial discharges (PDs) wave shapes using ultra wide band (UWB) techniques and its relation to the surface degradation produced on the surface of a single spherical void. The spherical void was occluded in epoxy resin at the time of molding the sample. The surface degradation was studied by optical and electron scanning microscopy (SEM) showing that the evolution of localized degradation was related to the pulse shape detected on the UWB system. These degradation zones evolved into a tree. This tree is also presented on optical microscopy photographs. Analysis of the wave shape at UWB can therefore correlate directly to ageing and ultimate failure of polymerical insulation.

articleTitle: Analysis of SF6/N2 gas mixture decomposition by-products in electric discharges
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Two methods have been carried out for the analysis of SF6/N2 gas mixture decomposition by-products in electric discharges: infrared spectroscopy and gas chromatography. The infrared spectroscopy is a rapid method from which we can have qualitative analysis about all the products in a mixture, except those having the same absorption lines. Besides, the gas chromatography needs more time and experiments than the infrared spectroscopy, but it is the best method to have quantitative analysis of each SF6/N2 by-product with precision. So, we would not discriminate any of these two analytical methods which are complementary.

articleTitle: The influence of electrotechnical papers technology on their specific partial discharges inception electric field
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In this paper, attention was focused on the real possibility in outlining the technology influence on the specific P.D. inception electric field of some electrotechnical papers. This kind of analysis takes the aim to direct applications regarding improved dielectric structures and can also complete the theory of cellulose dielectric failure.

articleTitle: The propagation of a 4 metre guided discharge across a dielectric surface
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper describes a recently developed method which allows extremely long discharges (1-5 m) to be produced across dielectric surfaces. This is achieved by depositing charge on the surface of the material of interest which is subsequently discharged through the application of an impulse voltage.

articleTitle: Extended range dielectric spectroscopy of polyetheretherketone (PEEK)
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Complex relative permittivity data for polyetheretherketone (PEEK) obtained over the extended ranges from 0.1 Hz to 3 MHz and -180 /spl deg/C to +230 /spl deg/C is discussed. It is concluded that dielectric relaxations in PEEK arise variously from local-mode segmental motions, group ring flips, Brownian motion associated with the glass transition, and MWS polarizations at interfaces between crystalline and amorphous domains.

articleTitle: Partial discharge measurement and gas monitoring of a power transformer on-site
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In this paper, the observation of a power transformer in a substation with the help of gas monitoring and Partial Discharge (PD) measurement on-site is described. For the gas monitoring, a measuring system is installed, which records continuously the appearing undissolved gases of the transformer with a high resolution. Thus, it is possible to observe the gassing activity of the transformer accurately enough for an assessment. The simultaneous PD measurement is conducted with a broadband measuring system. The signals are digitized and filtered to suppress the continuous, sinusoidal noises. Afterwards, the pulse shaped noises synchronous to the main are suppressed via an adaptive algorithm. The separation of the PD from the stochastically appearing pulse shaped noises takes place with the help of directional coupling and pattern recognition algorithms.

articleTitle: Pitfalls of partial discharge measurements on stator windings of turbine generators
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The last decade shows a growing interest in the monitoring of partial discharges in stator windings of turbine generators. By monitoring discharges, one can follow possible deterioration of the insulation and detect serious faults at an early stage. Unfortunately, for the monitoring of discharges during regular operation, the standard technique according to IEC270 is not applicable. The main reasons for this are the complex propagation of discharge signals through a stator winding and the presence of many EM-disturbance sources in a power plant. In this paper, these important pitfalls are discussed; it is shown that a standard pd-detector can only be used if preceded by a sophisticated front-end. We illustrate with measurements on operating generators how interference and cross-talk can be rejected.

articleTitle: DC electrical accelerated ageing tests on polyethylene insulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper reports on an on-going study into assessing the long term dc performance and reliability of moulded production joints used in submarine repeatered optic communication cable systems. Emphasis is being placed on using meaningful short term accelerated ageing tests, results of which can be extrapolated to service life and conditions. Electrical breakdown data from ramp and constant stress tests of production mouldings are presented along with thin film samples microtomed from various parts of mouldings. Bulk space charge measurements of aged samples are reported and their effect on failure data are discussed.

articleTitle: Potential decay interpretation on insulating films: necessity of combining charge injection and slow volume polarization processes
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We suggest that any interpretation of potential decay on insulating materials, especially at low fields, but not only, should carefully examine the hypothesis of slow polarization processes, often overlooked in the past. To verify this hypothesis, we achieved surface potential measurements on thin films of polypropylene and high density polyethylene, involving fields up to 10/sup 8/ V.m/sup -1/. We present here the first results of this study, concerning isothermal potential decay and potential profiles.

articleTitle: Electrical rotating plant-condition monitoring
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The paper considers the application of Condition Monitoring Techniques to the HV electrical insulation of large electric motors and generators. A philosophy for condition monitoring is suggested. Examples of test techniques applicable are proposed with descriptions of their applicability and method of analysis.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction at high fields in oil-impregnated paper
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The conductivity of oil-impregnated paper was measured at applied fields of the order of 10/sup 7/ V m/sup -1/. The results, and those of similar investigations carried out by others, suggest that the mechanism of conduction is governed by the properties of the bulk material. The variation of conductivity with applied field measured experimentally is in broad conformity with that predicted by an existing theoretical analysis of bulk controlled conduction previously applied mainly, but not only, to polymers.

articleTitle: Measurement of conductor temperature of power cable by optical fiber sensor
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We conducted temperature measurements on the feeder cables of a substation for power distribution by using a distributed optical fiber sensor. As a result we confirmed that the hot point of a conduit with multiple lines installed can be determined with ease. Moreover, our calculations resulted in a maximum conductor temperature of 70/spl deg/C, which confirms that there still remains a tolerance of approximately 20/spl deg/C. Hereinafter, we will continue with our study in pursuit of a method that would allow to compute allowable currents by using the sensor mentioned above.

articleTitle: On spatial inhomogeneity of electric field in thin layer of dielectric liquid
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The model proposed is based on the measurement of resistivity to calculate the distribution of electric field in thin layer of dielectric liquids. This model was applied to investigate the spatial inhomogeneity of the electric field in benzene, toluene and carbone tetrachloride of high purity. The feature of behaviour of thin layer in the electric field must be taken into account in modelling the conduction process in dielectric liquids.

articleTitle: On the effect of space charges on breakdown strength by using two different injection methods
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The paper reports two different space charge injection methods and their effect on breakdown strength. Space charges were injected into a point-plane gap either using a corona pin arrangement external to the gap or by applying a dc voltage to the point electrode. It has been found that the two different space charges injection methods have the same effect on minimum impulse breakdown levels in both electron-attaching and non-attaching gases. The experimental evidence indicates that the initiatory electrons resulting from detachment have a great influence on the breakdown strength.

articleTitle: The measurement of charge trapping characteristics in high voltage insulation materials
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A Thermally Stimulated Current Spectrometer has been designed and built. The Spectrometer has been primarily developed to investigate the charge trapping behaviour of high voltage insulation materials. An initial study into the effect of antioxidant additive on the TSC spectra of LDPE has been completed and the results presented demonstrate the validity of the developed experiment.

articleTitle: The electric properties of an iron-kaolin functionally gradient material
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: An idea of gradient functions has recently developed in Japan, giving birth to an entirely new concept in materials. The formal name for the new materials is "functionally graded materials", or FGMs for short. Methods of manufacture of FGMs vary, but include the chemical and physical vapour deposition methods, the electrolytic deposition method, the atomised metal spray method, and a method in which powdered material is first melted in a plasma jet and then deposited. But none of these methods or other previously existing ones, has allowed the manufacture of a comprehensive range of FGM thicknesses extending from less than 1 millimetre to several centimetres. The authors have developed a new method of FGM manufacture, for which a US patent has been granted. Using this method, it has became possible to produce FGMs across the whole range of thickness from a few millimetres up to several tens of centimetres. We call this new method "successive layer accretion". The present paper is a report on measured electric properties of an iron-kaolin FGM, namely magnetic permeability, resistance, relative permittivity and transmission loss.

articleTitle: Development of energy storage capacitors, based on PVDF/BaTiO/sub 3/ films
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The influence of stretching, in the rubbery state and in the molten state, on the relative permittivity and the electric field strength of PVDF composite films for storage capacitors have been studied. The effect of a coupling agent is also examined.

articleTitle: An estimate of the fractal dimension of water trees
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Water trees are regions of microcavitation and filamentary damage in a polymer (such as XLPE) caused by the penetration of aqueous salts and the presence of an electric field. They appear in the insulation of service power cables and can lead to electrical failure. The ramified visual aspect of water trees suggests underlying fractal characteristics. The calculation of the fractal dimension can help to confirm the fractal character and to understand the physical mechanisms that lead to water tree formation and growth. In this paper two types of experimental images of water trees have been investigated: (i) methylene blue stained water tree images obtained with the help of optical microscopy; (ii) images obtained using SEM (scanning electron microscopy).

articleTitle: Conductivity of polyethylene induced by pulsed UV light, fast electrons and X-rays
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Current transients induced in low density polyethylene (LDPE) are studied. The mobility of holes has been found to be 2.7/spl times/10/sup -6/ m/sup 2/ V/sup -1/ s/sup -1/ below the glassy transition point T/sub g/ of LDPE and 6.3/spl times/10/sup -6/ m/sup 2/ V/sup -1/ s/sup -1/ above it. Conductivity activation energy has been defined as 0.013 eV below T/sub g/ and 0.029 eV above it. Memory effect with anomalous reverse current flow was found in the sample coated with semitransparent Au electrodes for UV flash excitation. The occurrence of micro-discharges during thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) recording, in a previously electron beam treated sample is reported.

articleTitle: Density dependence on negative corona onset voltage in helium
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper presents the results of experiments in gaseous helium, in point cathode-plane geometry, for a wide range of densities (3.10/sup 19/-2.10/sup 21/) cm/sup -3/. A current instability occurs at a threshold voltage V/sub S/. For V>V/sub S/, a space charge limited current is observed. The nature of charge carriers deduced from their mobility value and the variation of V/sub S/ with density is discussed as a function of helium purity.

articleTitle: The effect of surface charge on the performance of cast resin insulation for gas insulated substations
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The maximum charge densities which can exist on the surface of a conical barrier are calculated, and it is shown how these vary with voltage and location. An experimental rig is constructed which allows conical barriers, of similar dimensions to those of many manufacturers, to be stressed by a DC voltage. The maximum voltage available is approximately equal to 1 p.u for a 420 kV system, thus reproducing the trapped charge conditions found after switching operations on isolated sections of busbar in a 420 kV GIS. It is shown that charge present on the concave surface of the barrier significantly lowers the barrier flashover voltage. The charging conditions required for surface flashover vary across the barrier and this is attributed to differences in the surface conductivity. The track marks generated are similar in appearance to those previously reported and occur across the convex surface of the barrier. They originate at the outer triple junction. The direction and location of the flashovers are explained by analysing the field distribution across the barrier with charge present on its concave surface.

articleTitle: An investigation into the factors affecting space charge in XLPE
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper discusses the results of an on-going study using pressure wave propagation (PWP) to investigate the space charge characteristics of cross linked polyethylene (XLPE) under dc electric stress. Emphasis is placed on quantitative appraisal of calibration and verification procedures which can have marked effects on measured parameters and resultant estimates of space charge densities and electric stress distribution.

articleTitle: The system for complex electric permittivity measurements of solid-state materials in the range of 20 Hz to 1 GHz
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We worked out a fully computerised system for complex electric permittivity measurements of solid-state materials in the frequency range of 20 Hz to 1 GHz and temperature from 77 K to 430 K. The measuring system contains three main parts: (i) metrological, (ii) temperature controller, (iii) sample holder with a specially designed Dewar container and a level controller of liquid nitrogen.

articleTitle: Improvement of measurement techniques in PD pulse detection in large HV equipment
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Partial discharge (PD) measurement has been used as a tool to assess insulation integrity for many years. In terms of detection of PD pulses, a proper assessment of insulation integrity relies on accurate acquisition of the PD pulse signal. However, measurement errors may arise due to the measurement facilities involved. This paper discusses one aspect of the measurement system, the role of connecting cables. It is shown that the connecting cables used in PD measurement may distort PD waveforms recorded. Attenuation, reflection, resonance, and coupling occur in coaxial cables for transmission of RF/UHF signals.

articleTitle: A simple optical method for measuring currents at high voltages with an example of use on a coronating electrode in air
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: An inexpensive system is described for measuring currents up to a few amperes with a resolution of 0.1 /spl mu/A in high-voltage conductors. The system uses an optical-fibre link which provides excellent electrical isolation. An application to electrostatic precipitators is described.

articleTitle: Modelling of TSDC spectra: the effect of local fields
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The modifications to the authors' polarisation and thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) simulations successfully produce TSDC spectra with two distinct peaks. The interactions between two charged species with differing mobilities are complex. However it is still possible to derive activation energies with reasonable accuracy using either an Arrhenius plot of the initial current rise or by examining the shift in peak position with differing temperature ramp-rates. Altering the form of the charge distribution in the region close to the electrodes seems however to have a significant effect on the activation energy derived using an Arrhenius plot indicating a field or concentration gradient driven effect.

articleTitle: Frequency and field roles in water absorption in composite dielectrics
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Consisting of more than one material and having internal interfaces, composite insulators are susceptible to water ingress. It has been shown previously that the absorption of water is increased in the presence of an electric field. This paper presents results of more recent work done on this subject. It was found that the frequency of the applied field had a definite influence on water ingress and also that the quantity of absorbed water depended on the type of the interfacing material used in the composite dielectric. To study this aspect a number of experiments were performed using specimens of different composite dielectrics.

articleTitle: Variation of the dielectric properties of a multilayer stack of dry kraft paper with air pressure, mechanical pressure, temperature and time duration
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The dielectric properties of a multilayer stack of kraft paper depend on the frequency, the temperature, the mechanical pressure and its dwell time, and the air temperature. It takes over 3000 hours for the dielectric loss factor to attain a new steady value after a change in air pressure, and over 20 hours to reach a steady value after a change in temperature. These long-term effects are probably due to the slow diffusion of ions through the stack, particularly those held at the interfaces between sheets.

articleTitle: Description of a complex test programme for the evaluation of outdoor ageing-relevant properties of silicon rubber
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The paper deals with a research project, aimed at both, the selection of test procedures for evaluation of polymers and of a Silicon Rubber (SR) for composite hollow insulators for outdoor service use. The investigations are focused on the validation of the ageing resistance at simultaneous voltage and pollution layer stressing. To take account of the dynamic behaviour of SR, standardized and non-standardized procedures are applied to improve the transferability of the test results to the performance under outdoor conditions. The test procedures are discussed with corresponding results. The investigated SR-types were RTV2- and LSR-sytems.

articleTitle: Dielectric behaviour of some arylazo benzothiazine derivatives in relation to its microbial activity
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The dielectric loss /spl epsiv/" for some derivatives was measured in dioxane at 20/spl deg/C in the microwave region (0.2-18 GHz). The data were analyzed into two Debye terms ascribed to two relaxation processes. The first relaxation could be attributed to the rotation of the molecule as a whole while the second relaxation could be attributed to the flexibility of such molecules. In addition a third relaxation which is expected to be in the higher frequency range may be due to the Poley absorption resonance. This relaxation is reasonable for the liberation of dipoles damped by soft collisions. The static dielectric constant for the investigated compounds were measured and the dipole moments were determined. The biological activity of these compounds were tested against a wide range of microorganisms using the disc diffusion method and the minimum inhibitory concentration for the active compounds were determined. A correlation between the activity and the dielectric parameters were achieved.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation behaviour in supercooled short-chain primary amines
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This work presents the dielectric behaviour in the primary amines for the importance of NH/sub 2/ group it bears in the interaction of amino acids and proteins and their influence in the electric conduction process. Therefore, we have studied the dielectric properties for 1-propylamine, 1-butylamine and 1-pentylamine. Measurements were performed, between room temperature and -200/spl deg/C, in the low frequency range. The isofrequency recordings of dispersion /spl epsiv/' and absorption /spl epsiv/'', for these three primary amines, show clearly the liquid-solid phase transitions and the effect of the aliphatic chain length.

articleTitle: The liquid-solid interface: the effect of negative liquid discharge
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A study of the interaction of a negative discharge, propagating in a liquid dielectric, with a thin solid barrier has been made. Effects were sought under the headings of charge storage, thermal effects, and mechanical degradation. Charge accumulation was noted on polythene, evidenced by distortion of the propagating negative discharge, and by an unexpected back flash effect. Continued interaction of the negative discharge with a paper barrier caused progressive physical deterioration, evidenced by a reduction in the breakdown voltage. No significant thermal effects were evident.

articleTitle: The fractal nature of electrode polarization
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The electric model represents the simplest variant of the cell taking into account the effects of electrode polarization. It is possible to modify the model taking into account the more complex structure of the electrode fractal surface. To describe electrode polarization data the well-known Cole-Cole empirical formula has been used. The dependence of complex impedance vs. frequency has also been described by the Cole-Davidson formula. In order to understand these empirical expressions as a preliminary step, we can formulate the following problem: to construct an equivalent electric circuit which can model the electrode polarization phenomenon and give the complex impedances of Cole-Cole, Cole-Davidson and the more general Havriliyak-Negami formula.

articleTitle: Relationships between the nature of traps and dielectric properties of polymers obtained from mirror measurements
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In the field of space charge physics, the nature of traps and their role on charge effect and breakdown properties have not been well-established. In this paper, the contribution of "physical" and "chemical" defects on the trapping and detrapping properties of perfectly defined polymers is reported. First, the effects of "physical" traps, i.e. crystallinity ratio changes have been studied. Second, the effects of "chemical" traps, i.e. oxidised sites have been investigated. These latter defects have been created by UV irradiation resulting in a partial oxidation of polyethylene chain without morphological changes. The concentration of oxidised species has been evaluated using FTIR spectroscopy. The trapping ability and the traps depth of sample were studied using the Mirror-Image method. This technique allows us to study the trapping and detrapping properties of dielectric materials. Indeed, charging conditions can be perfectly controlled and modulated without using electrodes. This study demonstrates that the charging capacity of polymers is correlated to the crystallinity ratio. Secondly, it appears that oxidation strongly affects traps characteristics as seen by Mirror-Image method. Therefore, this study provides a better understanding of traps in polymers and their effects on space charge behaviour.

articleTitle: The measurements of piezoelectric properties of the lead zirconate titanate/polystyrene composites for thick transducers of acoustic waves
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The piezoelectric properties for the composite system of LZT ceramics and polystyrene have been studied. The experimental results for the dielectric, elastic, and piezoelectric constants are compared with the theoretical predictions.

articleTitle: Time domain dielectric spectroscopy, advantages and disadvantages
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Recent developments in high speed sampling techniques and digital processing, together with the basic theory of Time Domain Dielectric Spectroscopy (TDS), have brought about a new generation of TDS measurement systems. We describe such an instrument based on Time Domain Measuring Set (TDMS) specially designed for TDS hardware support. The system utilizes the difference method of measurement, and the registration of primary signals with parallel time nonuniform sampling.

articleTitle: Contribution to the qualitative and quantitative estimation of the PD effect on the surface layer of epoxy resins and composites
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Joint application of electron scanning profilometry, optical and scanning microscopy and of measurements of the Rs surface resistance has yielded promising results in investigations into partial discharges (PD) degradation processes of the surface layer of epoxy resins and composites. On the basis of the investigations it was possible, among others, to state that local changes in resistivity are not directly a consequence of changes in the epoxy surface profile. The results suggest instead the possible importance of deposits on the surface in modifying the resistivity. On the example of the Epidian 2 (Ep2) resin and its composite with the Al2O3 filler (Ep2K), this paper draws attention to some conditions which should be taken into account when the behaviour of the surface layer of a dielectric in various types of PD exposure is compared.

articleTitle: Degradation of oil-paper systems due to the electrical field enhanced absorption of water
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Oil-impregnated paper used as an insulating medium in oil-filled transformers degrades over a period of time. The degradation and resulting depolymerisation of the paper is caused by the absorption of water. The present investigation was undertaken with a view to quantifying the damage done to the paper by the water. For this purpose the tensile strength as well as the electrical strength of paper was measured as a function of the water content of the paper. The experiments consisted of a number of simple tests. Controlled amounts of de-ionised and ionised water were injected into the oil. The oil impregnated paper assembly was placed in the oil/water mixture for a fixed time and measurements of tensile and electrical strength were subsequently made.

articleTitle: Solid dielectric material considerations in the design of repetitive pulsed power transmission line systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Although solid insulation is generally considered to be non-recoverable in the event of dielectric breakdown, there are pulsed power applications where its use is warranted. This can result in increased system capacitance with the possibility of operating at increased energy levels or reduced system volumes. However solid insulation failure under pulsed power conditions is not fully understood. This paper reports on the results of a recent test programme, the object of which was to investigate the material limits of solid dielectric insulation at potentials in excess of 100 kV. This was a comparative study of various materials and was not an attempt to optimise the material breakdown voltage but to make a direct sample comparison under identical, representative pulsed power conditions.

articleTitle: Prediction of monopolar corona charge injection and current distribution in air for complex geometries
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A three-dimensional finite element (FE) modelling method has been devised to allow the development of software for predicting charge injection, current distribution and electric field due to monopolar corona discharge in air from electrodes with complex geometries. Prototype software using this method has given promising results. The motivation for the modelling method was the prediction of the effect of discharge electrode geometries on the performance of electrostatic precipitators (ESPs)-devices that remove solid and liquid particles from industrial gas flows. Therefore the method also has provision for the inclusion of the effects of an arbitrary background space charge (since precipitators contain charged airborne particulate). This paper gives an overview of the physical problem and the FE method used to solve it.

articleTitle: Dielectric and hygrothermal studies in rubber modified epoxy resins
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We report in this work the results of dielectric studies by means of thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) techniques and the results of hygrothermal studies on a series of rubber-modified epoxy resins, based on reaction of the diclycidyl ether of bisphenol A (DGEBA) with diaminodiphenyl methane (DDM). The rubber modifier used was a carboxyl terminated butadiene-acrylonitrile (CTBN) reactive oligomer.

articleTitle: Static electrification-chemical methods to suppress the charging behaviour in transformer oils
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The phenomenon of electrostatic charge generation due to friction between the flowing insulating liquid and the fixed solid insulation is well known. The increase in power and voltage ratings of transformers has made the static charge phenomenon an important parameter to be controlled to prevent transformer failures due to charge accumulations. To mitigate this problem of charge accumulations and to suppress the developed charge density in transformer oils, different methods, like, mixing low charging oils with high charging oils, use of additives like benzotriazole (BTA) have been suggested in the literature. In this paper, the authors studied the origin and manifestation of static electrification phenomenon of Indian Paraffinic oils by measuring the charge density of transformer oil base stock (TOBS) and oil samples drawn before clay treatment and oils as received in drums. The authors studied different chemical methods to suppress the charge density of oils by using different additives, like, triazoles, tetrazoles, imidazoles and high molecular weight alcohols. The authors also studied the charge suppression by blending oils with linear alkyl benzene (LAB) and processing with different adsorbents like molecular sieves, alumina, and fullers earth.

articleTitle: Dielectric relaxation spectroscopy in interpenetrating polymer networks
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The electrical and dielectric properties of Interpenetrating Polymer Networks (IPNs) based on crosslinked polyurethane (PUR) and copolymer of butylmethacrylate and dimethacrylate triethylene glycol were studied by means of broadband ac dielectric relaxation spectroscopy. Three relaxation processes were observed: secondary /spl beta/-relaxation (due to copolymer), /spl alpha/-relaxation due to the glass-rubber transition of PUR phase and conductivity current relaxation due to space charges trapped at the interfaces of the material with different conductivity. The dipolar mechanisms (/spl beta/,/spl alpha/) and the ac conductivity mechanism were studied in detail by analyzing the dielectric susceptibility data within the complex permittivity formalism, and modulus formalism. For the copolymer network the dielectric losses /spl epsi/"(/spl omega/) show a strong secondary /spl beta/-relaxation which becomes faster in the IPNs. The PUR network displays a relatively broad /spl alpha/-relaxation process which becomes slower in the IPNs. The energy and the shape parameters of the response were determined for both mechanisms at several temperatures.

articleTitle: The application of SbSI and other ferroelectric materials to the generation of solitons and shock waves on nonlinear high voltage transmission lines
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This paper describes the use of nonlinear ferroelectric materials for the generation of high voltage shock waves and solitons. A new material, SbSI, which has not previously been used in this field has been found to have particularly good nonlinear properties in comparison to other ferroelectric materials. Its nonlinear dielectric characteristics are described with special reference to the generation of high voltage shock waves and solitons.

articleTitle: Electrical properties of 12 /spl mu/m biaxially oriented poly(ethylene naphthalate 2,6 dicarboxylate) films related to ageing
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: PEN films have been irradiated by corona discharges in a global action cell in a plane to plane electrode configuration disposed in an oven, allowing different temperatures of irradiation, and thereby reproducing the working conditions of insulating systems, e.g. combined high temperature and a possible irradiation by partial discharges. Ageing under these conditions has been carried on for two hours. In a first part, a morphological determination of the surface of the films is presented. Since this morphology is shown to be the high temperature (/spl beta/) one, it has been used to explain dielectric relaxation measurements of samples aged at temperature near the high temperature crystallisation of 245/spl deg/C, assuming a phase transition process.

articleTitle: Polarization currents in high temperature polymers in 10/sup -6/-10s time range
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: While considerable data are available on the steady state currents under dc voltages in polymers, transient current measurements are relatively few. The transient currents resulting from the application of a step voltage are studied in aramid paper (Nomex(R)), aramid paper-mica composites and Fluoropolymer (Tefzel(R)) films. Experimental results are obtained in the temperature range of 50-200/spl deg/C at electric field strengths of 1.32 MVm/sup -1/ to 20 MVm/sup -1/. The currents are recorded in the time scale extending from 2/spl mu/s to 2s as measured from the edge of the step voltage. Initially transient currents decay with time. At 0.1s, currents in fluoropolymer start to increase with time, while the currents in aramid paper and composite continue to decrease. Possible mechanisms are considered. The conductivity is observed to be related to relaxation time.

articleTitle: Electrical field dependence of conductivity and critical exponent of it for carbon black-resin composites
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A large critical exponent of conductivity (t>2) and its field dependence of carbon black-polyethylene composites are discussed based on the fluctuation induced tunneling model (FIT model). Temperature dependence of conductivity is also discussed with a modified model, by introducing the effect of thermal expansion on a tunneling gap between carbon aggregates into the FIT model.

articleTitle: Observation of charge behavior in organic photoconductor using the pulsed electroacoustic method and pressure wave propagation method
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Recently, many methods to measure the space charge distribution in solid dielectrics have been developed, such as the laser-induced pressure wave propagation (LIPP) method by means of the pulse laser, the pressure wave propagation (PWP) method by means of the piezo-electric transducer, and the pulsed electroacoustic (PEA) method. In this report, the resolution of PWP method using a piezo-electric transducer as a generator of acoustic pulse wave has been improved. To improve the resolution, a new technique to generate the narrow acoustic wave was employed. In consequence of the usage of this new technique, we have succeed to obtain the resolution of about 10 /spl mu/m. The principle and the result of this technique will be introduced here. Furthermore, a typical measurement result of carrier generation, drift and trapping in an organic photoconductor (OPC) will be introduced and compared with the result obtained using PEA method.

articleTitle: Electrical tree growth in XLPE material under ac and impulse voltages
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The work reported in this paper deals with certain aspects of treeing in XLPE material. The influence of the presence of electrical trees on some of the electrical and physico-chemical properties of the XLPE material has been investigated. Impulse voltage withstand characteristics of XLPE samples degraded due to electrical tree growth has been discussed. The techniques employed for measurement and the relevance of various measurements has been presented.

articleTitle: High dose gamma irradiation effects in polyether-sulphone
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Polyethersulphone (PES) is a polymer exhibiting high-temperature chemical and mechanical stability derived from an aromatic functional group. Previous work has shown that after exposure to gamma radiation the electrical properties of PES were affected at high doses. We report here a more detailed investigation of the effect of dose on the dielectric properties of PES by measuring changes in both the low frequency dielectric (LFD) spectrum and the thermally stimulated discharge current (TSDC) spectrum using partial polarisation methods.

articleTitle: Characteristics of surface discharges on outdoor high voltage insulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: It was shown that discharges observed on the surfaces of wet insulators are not electric arcs but are a form of glow discharge operating at atmospheric pressure. These glows occur between electrodes consisting of water and contaminants forming an electrolyte. The resistance of an EPDM and a silicone rubber material to loss of hydrophobicity from surface discharge activity was evaluated using a novel technique. It was found that silicone rubber was less resistant to surface discharges than EPDM. It was also found that low current discharges with average currents of less than 2 mA produced more rapid loss of hydrophobicity than larger discharges.

articleTitle: Using partial discharge techniques to characterise transformer oil
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The breakdown arc of a negative discharge is preceded by a burst of current pulses. Near to breakdown this burst of current pulses gives information about the size of the discharge and can be used to map its development. This paper develops the idea that, with the advent of fast digitizing oscilloscopes, the recording of such current pulse bursts can provide an alternative approach to the testing of insulating oils. The standard electrical breakdown test for transformer oil continues to be employed for the want of a better test, although it is acknowledged that the information it gives is of limited value. The proposed alternative approach, by avoiding actual breakdowns and testing over a longer period, can give more reliable (and reproducible) information not only about the breakdown voltage but also about the particle content of the oil.

articleTitle: A diffusion limited mechanism to explain current pulse rate in a pre-breakdown current burst in silicone fluids
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Measurements have been made of prebreakdown cavity growth and of the accompanying current pulse bursts in silicone fluids over a range of viscosities from 0.65 cSt to 1000 cSt. At high viscosities the average time between pulses (/spl delta/t) is proportional to fluid viscosity, but in the low viscosity limit the dependence is nearer to square root of viscosity. To explain this viscosity dependence we make use of the fact that a pulse cannot occur until charge from the previous pulse has been effectively removed. We consider two possible mechanisms of charge dissipation, namely (i) ion detrapping and drift in the applied field, and (ii) diffusion of an electronegative impurity species to the cavity interface, charge capture to create a mobile ion, and its subsequent drift in the field. For case (i) ion drift is the rate limiting process and this leads to /spl delta/t being proportional to viscosity. For case (ii), the diffusion limited case, /spl delta/t is proportional to the cube root of viscosity. This and other evidence inclines us to the diffusion limited model in the low viscosity limit.

articleTitle: Non-exponential dynamics in the microemulsions near the percolation threshold from time domain dielectric spectroscopy
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A percolation phenomenon is found in microemulsions when the water fraction, the temperature, the pressure, or the ratio of water to the surfactant was varied. Below the percolation onset, where the microemulsion has a structure of spherical droplets, the main contribution in the relaxation mechanism comes from the fast relaxation processes with characteristic relaxation times less than 1 ns. The processes are inherent to the dynamics of the single droplet components. In the percolation region transient clusters of a fractal nature are formed because of attractive interactions between droplets. An interpretation of the results was done in the framework of the dynamic percolation model. According to this model, near the percolation threshold, in addition to the fast relaxation related to the dynamics of droplet components, there are at least two much longer characteristic time scales. The longest process has characteristic relaxation times greater than a few microseconds and should be associated with the rearrangements of the typical percolation cluster. The temporal window of the intermediate process is a function of temperature. This intermediate process reflects the cooperative relaxation phenomenon associated with the transport of charge carriers along the percolation cluster. The purpose of this work is to further investigate the fractal dynamics of this cooperative relaxation process in microemulsions near the percolation threshold.

articleTitle: An optical fibre-based acoustic sensor for detecting electrical discharges in SF/sub 6/ puffer circuit breakers
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The optical fibre sensor employed to monitor the acoustic emissions utilizes laser speckle produced by multi-mode optical fibres, a technique known as fibredyne interferometry. This contribution will describe the optical sensing system and the experiments undertaken on a 145 kV SF/sub 6/ puffer circuit breaker test bed, and will provide some preliminary analysis of these results.

articleTitle: Analysis of electrical treeing process by discharge luminous image and discharge magnitude in each phase angle area
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This research was performed to analyze the treeing phenomena with a needle shape void by the discharge luminous quantity and the discharge magnitude. The discharge pulses and discharge luminescence were measured by the original measurement system for measuring the discharge magnitude and the discharge luminous image according to several phase angle area of the applied voltage. The luminous image was digitized to the luminous quantity with a computer after the experiment.

articleTitle: The use of TDDS for investigation of structural and dynamic behavior of protein molecules in aqueous solution
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The use of time domain dielectric spectroscopy (TDDS) for the investigation of protein structure and dynamic behavior in solution seems to us suitable since this method permits us to obtain the information about the relaxation processes, associated with the intramolecular motions and Brownian tumbling as a whole. It is known that in the native state the protein represents a reasonably rigid packed globule. However, under the effect of external conditions, the structure of protein can undergo essential changes. Under the influence of temperature, denaturants, pH of solution, etc., the globule structure can be transformed into a disordered coil. The applications of TDDS measurements to dynamic structure investigation during different conformational transitions of proteins are presented.

articleTitle: DC component of AC charging current of polyethylene insulated systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The purpose of this work is the performance of suitable measuring system, measurement of constant component in the needle-plane system having polyethylene insulation and description of the influence of different polyethylene insulation on that component. The presented system allows measurements of DC component of AC charging current of value 10/sup -13/ A. That measuring sensitivity of the system is ensured at voltages up to about 15 kV which is sufficient for testing the insulation systems for mean rated voltage.

articleTitle: Influence of compacting conditions on iron dielectromagnetic materials properties
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: The physical and mechanical performances of iron-resin composites can be suited to meet the needs of particular applications by the proper selection of iron particle size, resin content and also of compacting conditions (temperature, pressure). The total plastic content can be also adjusted, a lower plastic content yields to higher pressed density and higher plastic contents improve strength and high frequency performances. From the compacting point of view (pressure and pressing temperature) these must be chosen with regard to acceptable limits for resistivity, remanent induction and permeability. The increase in density and resistivity provided by warm compacting process yields to improved magnetic properties and so to good performances for frequency applications.

articleTitle: Dielectric behavior of a thermotropic liquid crystal incorporated in a porous glass
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: We present measurements of the dielectric constant in a composite system where a thermotropic liquid crystal is incorporated in a silica aerogel. In particular we discuss the observed features in the temperature dependence of /spl epsiv/'/sub L/ (T), the real part of the dielectric constant measured at low frequency. /spl epsiv/'/sub L/ (T) is smaller than the orientational average of the uniaxial anisotropic dielectric constant of the bulk. After rescaling, /spl epsiv/'/sub L/(T) well approximates the temperature dependence of the bulk dielectric behavior. This fact strongly suggests that the silica to liquid crystal interaction is strong and it enables to estimate the total silica surface.

articleTitle: Empirical treatment of high field conduction
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: High direct fields in thick dielectric materials produce often linear plots between log J vs /spl radic/E or log /spl sigma/ vs /spl radic/E, where E is the field (or voltage V) applied to the specimen, J is the current density and /spl sigma/ is the conductivity. Usually such linearity is attributed either to the Schottky electrode-limiting process or the Frenkel-Poole bulk-limiting process involving thermal emission assisted by the electric field E. In the present paper a Brownian model is used to represent real conduction situations. It offers a uniform field solution to a complex set of oil impregnated experiments.

articleTitle: Dielectric investigations of microphase separation in polyurethane-styrene/acrylonitrile blends
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This work deals with dielectric studies of microphase separation in blends of thermoplastic polyurethanes (TPUs) styrene/acrylonitrile (SAN) copolymers. The dielectric techniques used include broadband ac dielectric relaxation spectroscopy (DRS)-in frequency range of 10/sup 2/ to 10/sup 6/ Hz and temperature range of 200 to 450 K and thermally stimulated depolarization currents (TSDC) techniques. TSDC techniques were mainly employed to investigate the sub-glass local relaxations in TPU, SAN and their blends. DRS allowed to follow the dynamics of the glass transition in the pure components and and their blends. The /spl alpha/-relaxation due to the glass-rubber transition of the TPU phase becomes faster with increasing SAN content. On the other hand, the /spl alpha/-relaxation due to the glass-rubber transition in SAN becomes slower with increasing TPU content. These results are in agreement with glass transition measurements by calorimetry (DSC). The shape of dielectric loss peak for the primary /spl alpha/-relaxation of SAN does not change significantly with temperature and blend composition.

articleTitle: Avalanche and streamer formation in N/sub 2/ and dry air
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: This work deals with a time-resolved study of the avalanche and streamer formation phases leading to breakdown in atmospheric nitrogen and dry air. We present the results obtained from experiments and two-dimensional model simulations. It is shown what processes are responsible for the formation of a cathode directed streamer. The trends of externally measured quantities correspond with those predicted by our model.

articleTitle: Comparative tests of impulse strength of PE and XLPE insulation
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: In order to decrease losses in insulation the construction changes in cables are designed to introduce insulation materials boasting a decreased dielectric losses coefficient. For this reason PE and XLPE insulation is used in numerous applications, with users taking advantage of its good operating parameters and environmental protection. Insulation of constant voltage appliances is highly polarised and is also subjected to overvoltage. This can adversely affect the reliability of the line. That is why the present comparative tests of the influence of time and polarisation tension upon PE and XLPE impulse strength have been conducted.

articleTitle: Electrical conduction in polyimide thin films prepared by vapor deposition polymerization
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Electrical conduction in polyimide (PI) prepared by vapor deposition polymerization is investigated with a low frequency sinusoidal wave and saw-tooth shaped wave. The sinusoidal response shows a asymmetric current wave form (with respect to t-axis) which depends on the electrode materials. Current wave forms observed with saw-tooth shaped wave voltage show a peak associated with space-charges.

articleTitle: The behaviour and interaction of monopolar current plumes from points on discharge electrodes in air
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Some devices such as electrostatic precipitators (ESPs) have electrodes for producing corona discharge in air. Corona discharge in air is also a common but unwanted phenomenon in high-voltage equipment and distribution systems. The measurements presented in this paper are for monopolar corona from discharge electrodes suspended between parallel earthed plates (such as those found in an ESP). A corona discharge electrode injects charge into air through a field-driven electron avalanche mechanism in the region of partial breakdown surrounding the high-voltage electrodes. The injection is space-charge limited resulting in an approximately fixed field at the electrode at voltages above corona inception.

articleTitle: Evaluation of X-ray induced partial discharge technique for epoxy resin insulation systems
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: A series of experiments are described which evaluate the suitability of the X-ray Induced Partial Discharge (XIPD) technique to obtain improved PD characterisation of epoxy resin insulation systems and to determine its potential for locating the position of internal discharge sites in these insulators.

articleTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No.430)

articleTitle: Reproducibility, traceability and uncertainty of dielectric measurements using automated vector network analysis
publicationTitle: Seventh International Conference on Dielectric Materials, Measurements and Applications (Conf. Publ. No. 430)
abstract: Methods for determining the residual directivity and linearity in an HP8510C based dielectric measurement system are examined. A comparison is made between estimating the linearity from multiple calibrated fixed attenuators and by a fixed frequency step attenuator. The effect of calibration technique is also investigated by measuring the linearity following both sliding load and thru-reflect-line methods.
